source.text:
# Keep Web Preview In One Window

Keep Windows WebView previews inside the GPUI application window. Move WebView2
work to a dedicated STA worker that owns a private child-window host inside the
main window, and prevent native floating surfaces from competing with that child
window.

The result must retain one application top-level window across resize and close
transitions. Reject approaches that create a companion window or blank the
preview whenever an overlay appears.

understood_intent.stated_goal: Keep Windows WebView previews inside one GPUI application window.
relevant_context: The design uses a dedicated Windows STA worker and a private child-window host inside the main window.
constraints: A companion window, overlay-triggered blanking, or a second top-level application window violates the prompt.
non_goals: Do not split the preview into a companion window.
understood_intent.expected_deliverable: A single-window WebView design that remains stable through resize and close transitions.
success_evidence: One application top-level window survives resize and close transitions without blanking the active preview.
unresolved_decisions: Should native visual integration around the active WebView be stated as an explicit revision requirement?

clarification_questions.question: Should native visual integration around the active WebView be stated as an explicit revision requirement?
clarification_questions.impact: The answer determines whether overlay-free native chrome becomes part of the proposed wording.

answers.answer: Yes. Require the WebView to remain inside the single GPUI window and appear integrated with native, overlay-free chrome.
